title: Fourth opinion: Vázquez and Alfonso de Castro, no wholly good moral work without grace
source_text: XIX. Attamen in Schola Romana reperiuntur non pauci qui affirmant nullum opus morale ex omni circumstantia bonum posse fieri sine auxilio gratiae. Haec est sententia Gabrielis Vasques in primam secundae tomo secundo disputatione centesima & nonagesima. Ubi pro se plurimos citat ex Scholasticis, tam veteribus quam recentioribus, Et inter alios Alphonsum a Castro, qui hanc assertionem ut Catholicam ponit, Liberum hominis arbitrium ex sola sua potestate, addita etiam illa communi & generali Dei concausatione, non potest sine aliquo Dei speciali auxilio bonum aliquod operari, quoniam semper circa illud praecedit quaedam monitio, aut attractio, aut inspiratio, aut aliquod donum naturae superadditum, quod ipse Deus mere gratis, quibus illi placet, donat. Libro septimo adversus haereses. Verbo Gratia: haeresi 1. assertione 3.
pass_a_gloss: XIX. Yet in the Roman School are found not a few who affirm that no moral work good in every circumstance can be done without the help of grace. This is the opinion of Gabriel Vasques on the first of the second tome two disputation one hundred and ninety. Where he cites for himself very many from the Scholastics, both old and more recent, And among others Alphonsus a Castro, who sets down this assertion as Catholic, The free choice of man from its own power alone, added even that common and general concausation of God, cannot without some special help of God work any good, since always concerning it there precedes some admonition, or attraction, or inspiration, or some gift superadded to nature, which God himself gives purely freely, to whom it pleases him. Book seven against heresies. Under the word Grace: heresy 1. assertion 3.
pass_b_english: Yet not a few in the Roman School affirm that no moral work good in every circumstance can be done without the help of grace. This is Gabriel Vázquez's view on the Prima Secundae, vol. 2, disputation 190. There he cites very many Schoolmen, older and more recent, on his side.

Among them is Alfonso de Castro, who lays down as Catholic the assertion: 'Man's free choice, by its own power alone, even with God's common and general co-causation added, cannot do any good without some special help from God. For every such good is always preceded by some warning, drawing, inspiration, or some gift added over and above nature, which God himself gives purely as a gift to whom he pleases.' Adversus haereses, book 7, under 'Grace', heresy 1, assertion 3.

choices.why: Grace given for a particular act, distinguished from God's general concurrence with all causes; 'help' keeps the scholastic auxilium.
